s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of neurological deficits with reduced consciousness, aphasia, and urinary incontinence in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions on brain CT scan
key_facts: 60-year-old woman
Recently diagnosed with HIV
Not yet on antiretroviral therapy
One-day history of reduced consciousness, aphasia, and urinary incontinence
Two-day history of dry cough, drenching night sweats, and weight loss
No fever, headache, neck stiffness, visual disturbances, photophobia, or seizures
Wasted appearance with weight of 40 kg
Afebrile with blood pressure 120/74 mmHg, pulse 66 beats/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14/15 with dysarthria
CD4 count of 6 cells/mm^3
Positive serum cryptococcal antigen test with a titer of 1:320

shortlist.label: Cryptococcal meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive serum cryptococcal antigen test and multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions on brain CT scan

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with neurological deficits and multiple ring-enhancing lesions on brain CT scan

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with neurological deficits and multiple enhancing lesions on brain CT scan

shortlist.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with neurological deficits and multiple white matter lesions on brain CT scan

shortlist.label: CNS tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with neurological deficits, weight loss, and night sweats

raw.rationale: The patient has a positive serum cryptococcal antigen test with a titer of 1:320, a very low CD4 count of 6 cells/mm^3, and multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions with significant peri-lesional edema, which are consistent with cryptococcal meningitis, especially in an HIV-positive patient not yet on antiretroviral therapy.

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: While toxoplasmosis is a common opportunistic infection in HIV-positive patients, the presence of a positive serum cryptococcal antigen test and the specific imaging findings make it less likely.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: This condition is less likely given the acute presentation and the specific laboratory and imaging findings that point towards an infectious cause.

rejected.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not align well with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, which typically presents with progressive neurological decline and characteristic white matter lesions without mass effect or enhancement.

rejected.label: CNS tuberculosis
rejected.why: While CNS tuberculosis is a possibility in an HIV-positive patient, the combination of a positive cryptococcal antigen test, the specific neuroimaging findings, and the lack of other suggestive features of tuberculosis make it less likely.
